pairs.question: Da mi, optuma femina, manum. Vbi ea est? quis ea est nam optuma?
pairs.derivation: Megadorus addresses Eunomia as optuma femina and asks for her hand; she asks who this best woman is (Vbi ea est? quis ea est nam optuma?), and he answers Tu. The setup line Da mi, optuma femina, manum is kept verbatim so optuma has its referent. Answer stops at Tu; what follows is Eunomia's incredulous Tune ais?, a new exchange.

pairs.question: Dic mihi, quali me arbitrare genere prognatum?
pairs.derivation: Megadorus asks Euclio what stock he thinks him born of; Euclio answers Bono. Clean one-word reply; what follows (Quid fide? Bona.) is the next question in the series.

pairs.question: Cur igitur poscis meam gnatam tibi?
pairs.answer: Vt propter me tibi sit melius mihique propter te et tuos.
pairs.derivation: Euclio asks why Megadorus seeks his daughter; Megadorus answers with a purpose clause (Vt propter me tibi sit melius...). Answer ends at the full stop before tuos.; next line begins Euclio's new speech Venit hoc mihi, Megadore, in mentem.

pairs.question: Quin cum it dormitum, follem obstringit ob gulam. Cur?
pairs.answer: Ne quid animae forte amittat dormiens.
pairs.derivation: Pythodicus says the miser ties a bag over his throat when he goes to sleep (Quin cum it dormitum, follem obstringit ob gulam); Anthrax asks Cur?, and Pythodicus answers Ne quid animae forte amittat dormiens. The verbatim setup line is kept so the bare interrogative Cur? has its referent. Answer is the direct purpose clause; next line is Anthrax's Etiamne obturat inferiorem gutturem, a new question.

pairs.question: Volo ego ex te scire qui sit agnus curio.
pairs.answer: Quia ossa ac pellis totust, ita cura macet.
pairs.derivation: Megadorus says he wants to know why the lamb is a curio (skinny); Euclio answers Quia ossa ac pellis totust, ita cura macet. Speech tag Volo ego ex te scire is a question of the indirect type; answer stops at the full stop before quin exta inspicere, which elaborates further.
